about.title: About Me
about.intro:
My path into videography started early—from a simple fascination with images, movement, and stories. During middle school I realized I was drawn not just to watching films but to understanding how they’re made. Camera angles, editing, rhythm, sound design—the tiny details that decide whether a video is just seen or truly felt.
That curiosity quickly became more than a hobby. I chose to attend a film and media school, where I’m currently completing my Abitur. There I deepen both the technical and creative sides of image making, storytelling, and production. At the same time, I learned fast that videography is mastered by doing—through practice and personal projects.
Alongside school, I gained hands-on experience at a media agency in Berlin. I saw the full lifecycle of professional productions—from the first idea through planning and shoot to post. That time taught me how vital structure, teamwork, and a sharp visual eye are to turn an idea into a finished film.
Today I handle my own projects and produce for clients and personalities including The Meat Company, Michael Smolik, and several ESN athletes. I also worked on a short film project with Abdu—known online as “The Voice Man” for his deep, thoughtful content on TikTok and Instagram.
Videography isn’t just a job or hobby for me. I can spend hours on camera settings, lighting, composition, or sound design—and happily lose myself perfecting small edit details until everything clicks. That “nerdy” side of image and sound is what drives me.
At 19, I independently produce videos, develop concepts, plan shoots, and deliver projects from idea to final film. My goal is to tell visual stories that don’t just look good but also carry something—a mood, an energy, or a personality.
And this is only the beginning.
